All-digital PLL: TDC and DCO quantization noise are the same ISF bookkeeping

Prerequisites: pll_noise_budget (the five-source budget, the in-band floor SrefN2+ScpS_{ref}N^2+S_{cp}Sref​N2+Scp​, the four-step derivation of the fractional-N ΔΣ third term), varactor_tuning_supply_pushing (the voltage → frequency → integrate-to-phase pipeline KVCO2Sv/Δf2K_{VCO}^2S_v/\Delta f^2KVCO2​Sv​/Δf2), sampling_pll (the other way of kicking the divider out of the loop) | Next: clock_chain_budget, serdes_clocking_connection, exercises

What this page answers​

The budget table in pll_noise_budget has five analog noise sources: reference, PFD/charge-pump, divider, loop filter, VCO. Over the past two decades, however, the mainstream has increasingly become the ADPLL (all-digital PLL): the "PFD + charge-pump + analog loop filter" is replaced by a TDC (time-to-digital converter — a circuit that measures the time difference between two edges as an integer) plus a digital loop filter, and the VCO is replaced by a DCO (digitally controlled oscillator — tuned by a bank of switched capacitors instead of a continuous varactor voltage). This page answers:

  1. How much in-band phase noise does the TDC's finite time resolution Δtres\Delta t_{res}Δtres​ become? It is the digital stand-in for the charge-pump's ScpS_{cp}Scp​, sits in the same slot of the budget table, but its magnitude is set by "quantization" rather than by electronic noise.
  2. How much out-of-band phase noise does the DCO's finite frequency resolution Δfres\Delta f_{res}Δfres​ become? It is the digital stand-in for the VCO and follows the varactor page pipeline "frequency error → integrate to phase → 1/Δf21/\Delta f^21/Δf2".
  3. How does ΔΣ dithering shape the DCO LSB away? This is the (1−z−1)m(1-z^{-1})^m(1−z−1)m shaping already derived in pll_noise_budget, reused in a new place.
  4. How the budget equation is rewritten: Sout=(SrefN2+STDC)∣Hlp∣2+(SDCO+Svco)∣Hhp∣2S_{out}=(S_{ref}N^2+S_{TDC})\lvert H_{lp}\rvert^2+(S_{DCO}+S_{vco})\lvert H_{hp}\rvert^2Sout​=(Sref​N2+STDC​)∣Hlp​∣2+(SDCO​+Svco​)∣Hhp​∣2, and why a 10 ps TDC makes the whole in-band budget lose to an ordinary charge-pump.

External-literature statement: the ADPLL architecture and the two standard formulas for TDC and DCO quantization noise are not in the 5 PDFs downloaded for this site (external literature, not among this site's 5 PDFs). Classic sources: R. B. Staszewski, J. L. Wallberg, S. Rezeq, C.-M. Hung, O. E. Eliezer, S. K. Vemulapalli, C. Fernando, K. Maggio, R. Staszewski, N. Barton, M.-C. Lee, P. Cruise, M. Entezari, K. Muhammad, and D. Leipold, "All-Digital PLL and Transmitter for Mobile Phones," IEEE J. Solid-State Circuits, vol. 40, no. 12, pp. 2469–2482, Dec. 2005, doi:10.1109/JSSC.2005.857417; R. B. Staszewski and P. T. Balsara, All-Digital Frequency Synthesizer in Deep-Submicron CMOS, Wiley, 2006 (equation numbers in both to be verified). The derivations on this page are fully self-contained: both formulas are derived step by step from "uniform quantization error → whitening → into the same integrator", identical to the site's existing ΔΣ four steps and the varactor pipeline; all numbers are marked illustrative.

Physical intuition (conclusion first): the TDC "rounds" the phase error to the nearest Δtres\Delta t_{res}Δtres​ and rolls that die once per reference period — this is a white phase-error source sampled at fRf_RfR​, sitting exactly in the PFD's seat, low-passed by the loop and, like the reference, an in-band floor; its magnitude depends only on Δtres/TV\Delta t_{res}/T_VΔtres​/TV​ (the quantization step as a fraction of one output period), independent of NNN. The DCO rounds the control word to the nearest Δfres\Delta f_{res}Δfres​ — a white frequency-error source sitting in the VCO's seat, high-passed by the loop; frequency error must be integrated once to become phase, so it looks like the VCO's 1/f21/f^21/f2 skirt but is set by the "quantization step" rather than by device noise. Neither newcomer is "electronic noise" — both are bit counts the designer chooses. The term that ISF theory is responsible for (the DCO's own device noise Γrms2/qmax2\Gamma_{rms}^2/q_{max}^2Γrms2​/qmax2​) is unchanged; it simply gains two quantized neighbours.

Step 1: ADPLL block diagram and the three noise entry points​

Three things first, because the "no N2N^2N2" below depends entirely on them:

  • Phase in an ADPLL is counted in "VCO cycles". Every reference period adds the "cycles that should have accumulated" RRR_RRR​ (the running sum of the frequency command word, which may be fractional); a counter counts how many cycles the DCO actually ran, RVR_VRV​ (an integer); the TDC supplies the sub-cycle fraction ε=Δt/TV\varepsilon=\Delta t/T_Vε=Δt/TV​ (Δt\Delta tΔt is the time from the reference edge to the next CKV edge, TV=1/f0T_V=1/f_0TV​=1/f0​ is the DCO period). The phase error ϕE=RR−RV−ε\phi_E=R_R-R_V-\varepsilonϕE​=RR​−RV​−ε is in output cycles; times 2π2\pi2π it is rad of output phase — this is the same fact as "the error is counted in VCO cycles to begin with" in the ΔΣ third term of pll_noise_budget, so TDC noise is likewise not multiplied by N2N^2N2.
  • No charge-pump, no analog loop filter. The ScpS_{cp}Scp​ and SlfS_{lf}Slf​ terms disappear, replaced by the TDC quantization STDCS_{TDC}STDC​. The digital loop filter itself adds no noise (finite-word-length effects are a separate matter).
  • The DCO is controlled by a bank of switched unit capacitors. The frequency step of the finest bank, Δfres\Delta f_{res}Δfres​, is the "quantization step"; the DCO's device noise (tank loss, active devices) is exactly the VCO's and is still set by the ISF: Svco∝Γrms2/qmax2⋅Si/f2S_{vco}\propto\Gamma_{rms}^2/q_{max}^2\cdot S_i/f^2Svco​∝Γrms2​/qmax2​⋅Si​/f2.

Step 2: TDC quantization → in-band floor (four steps, exactly like the ΔΣ third term)​

A TDC quantizes Δt\Delta tΔt into an integer number of Δtres\Delta t_{res}Δtres​ using a chain of delay elements (typically an inverter chain). As long as the phase error is "busy" enough (fractional-N, or dithered), the quantization error can be treated as white noise (the concrete threshold for "busy enough", and what it looks like when it fails, are in the "Numerical verification" section below). Step by step:

(i) Uniform quantization error. The quantization error ete_tet​ is uniformly distributed over ±Δtres/2\pm\Delta t_{res}/2±Δtres​/2:

σt2=Δtres212[s2].\sigma_{t}^2=\frac{\Delta t_{res}^2}{12}\qquad[\text{s}^2].σt2​=12Δtres2​​[s2].

(The same uniform-distribution formula as σe2=Δ2/12\sigma_e^2=\Delta^2/12σe2​=Δ2/12 in the ΔΣ third term, except that Δ\DeltaΔ there is in "cycles" and here it is in "seconds".)

(ii) Time error → output phase. One output period TVT_VTV​ corresponds to 2π2\pi2π rad, so

ϕTDC=2π etTV⟹σϕ2=(2π)212(ΔtresTV)2[rad2].\phi_{TDC}=2\pi\,\frac{e_t}{T_V}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \sigma_\phi^2=\frac{(2\pi)^2}{12}\Big(\frac{\Delta t_{res}}{T_V}\Big)^2\qquad[\text{rad}^2].ϕTDC​=2πTV​et​​⟹σϕ2​=12(2π)2​(TV​Δtres​​)2[rad2].

This step is where the "no N2N^2N2" lives: TVT_VTV​ is the output period, so ϕTDC\phi_{TDC}ϕTDC​ is already rad of output phase. If you insist on referring it to the reference side (dividing by TR=NTVT_R=NT_VTR​=NTV​), you get ϕ/N\phi/Nϕ/N, and going back to the output requires ×N\times N×N (power ×N2\times N^2×N2) — which cancels exactly. The most common rookie budget mistake is to multiply it by N2N^2N2 once more (the same trap as step (iv) of the ΔΣ section in pll_noise_budget).

(iii) Whitening at fRf_RfR​. The TDC produces one sample per reference period; the white sequence's power σϕ2\sigma_\phi^2σϕ2​ spreads uniformly over ±fR/2\pm f_R/2±fR​/2 (two-sided bookkeeping) → density σϕ2/fR\sigma_\phi^2/f_Rσϕ2​/fR​ per Hz:

LTDC=(2π)212(ΔtresTV)21fR,STDC=2 LTDC=(2π)26(ΔtresTV)21fR\mathcal{L}_{TDC}=\frac{(2\pi)^2}{12}\Big(\frac{\Delta t_{res}}{T_V}\Big)^2\frac{1}{f_R},\qquad S_{TDC}=2\,\mathcal{L}_{TDC}=\frac{(2\pi)^2}{6}\Big(\frac{\Delta t_{res}}{T_V}\Big)^2\frac{1}{f_R}LTDC​=12(2π)2​(TV​Δtres​​)2fR​1​,STDC​=2LTDC​=6(2π)2​(TV​Δtres​​)2fR​1​

(STDCS_{TDC}STDC​ in rad2/Hz\text{rad}^2/\text{Hz}rad2/Hz, single-sided, referred to the output, before the loop). Factor-of-2 bookkeeping flag (flagged every time): the literature's customary 1/121/121/12 version is two-sided bookkeeping, which numerically equals the SSB L\mathcal{L}L (the 12\tfrac1221​ in L≈12Sϕ\mathcal{L}\approx\tfrac12S_\phiL≈21​Sϕ​ cancels the ×2\times2×2 of single-siding); this site's strict single-sided SϕS_\phiSϕ​ convention needs the ×2\times2×2 (giving 1/61/61/6). This is the same class of factor-of-2 issue as [P1] Eq.(21)'s /4 (SSB bookkeeping) vs the clean time-domain /2, and as the ΔΣ third term's 1/121/121/12 vs 1/61/61/6.

(iv) Into the loop. It sits in the PFD's seat, shares the path of SrefN2S_{ref}N^2Sref​N2 and is low-passed by the same ∣Hlp∣2\lvert H_{lp}\rvert^2∣Hlp​∣2; for f≪fnf\ll f_nf≪fn​ it is a flat floor (white, no shaping), flat all the way to fR/2f_R/2fR​/2. So the TDC is the ADPLL's "in-band floor setter" — just as the charge-pump is for the analog PLL.

Dimension check: (2π)2(2\pi)^2(2π)2 [rad²] ×(Δtres/TV)2\times(\Delta t_{res}/T_V)^2×(Δtres​/TV​)2 [s²/s² = dimensionless] ×1/fR\times1/f_R×1/fR​ [s = 1/Hz] =rad2/Hz=\text{rad}^2/\text{Hz}=rad2/Hz — checks out.

Worked example (Example 1: 10 ps and 20 ps TDCs vs the charge-pump floor)​

Example 1: f0=5f_0=5f0​=5 GHz (TV=200T_V=200TV​=200 ps), fR=50f_R=50fR​=50 MHz (N=100N=100N=100, as in Example 3 of pll_noise_budget). Find LTDC\mathcal{L}_{TDC}LTDC​ for Δtres=10\Delta t_{res}=10Δtres​=10 ps and 20 ps, compare with that page's in-band floor of −121.2-121.2−121.2 dBc/Hz, and then solve for "how fine must the TDC be to break even with the charge-pump".

Step-by-step substitution (10 ps):

  1. Quantization step as a fraction of the period: Δtres/TV=10/200=0.05\Delta t_{res}/T_V=10/200=0.05Δtres​/TV​=10/200=0.05; squared 2.5×10−32.5\times10^{-3}2.5×10−3 (dimensionless).
  2. Prefactor: (2π)2/12=39.478/12=3.290(2\pi)^2/12=39.478/12=3.290(2π)2/12=39.478/12=3.290 [rad²].
  3. Phase variance: 3.290×2.5×10−3=8.225×10−3 rad23.290\times2.5\times10^{-3}=8.225\times10^{-3}\ \text{rad}^23.290×2.5×10−3=8.225×10−3 rad2 (σϕ=90.7\sigma_\phi=90.7σϕ​=90.7 mrad, i.e. σt=Δtres/12=2.887\sigma_t=\Delta t_{res}/\sqrt{12}=2.887σt​=Δtres​/12​=2.887 ps rms).
  4. Spread over fRf_RfR​: 8.225×10−3/(5×107)=1.645×10−108.225\times10^{-3}/(5\times10^7)=1.645\times10^{-10}8.225×10−3/(5×107)=1.645×10−10 → LTDC=10log⁡10(1.645×10−10)=−97.8\mathcal{L}_{TDC}=10\log_{10}(1.645\times10^{-10})=-97.8LTDC​=10log10​(1.645×10−10)=−97.8 dBc/Hz.
  5. 20 ps: (Δtres/TV)2(\Delta t_{res}/T_V)^2(Δtres​/TV​)2 is 4 times larger (+6.02+6.02+6.02 dB) → −91.8-91.8−91.8 dBc/Hz.

Result and interpretation: a 10 ps TDC gives a flat in-band floor of −97.8-97.8−97.8 dBc/Hz, 23.4 dB above the analog PLL's −121.2-121.2−121.2 dBc/Hz (reference×N2\times N^2×N2 + CP). Solving backwards: for LTDC\mathcal{L}_{TDC}LTDC​ to equal 7.5×10−137.5\times10^{-13}7.5×10−13 (i.e. −121.2-121.2−121.2 dBc/Hz) requires Δtres=TV12 L fR/(2π)=0.675\Delta t_{res}=T_V\sqrt{12\,\mathcal{L}\,f_R}/(2\pi)=0.675Δtres​=TV​12LfR​​/(2π)=0.675 ps — finer than a single inverter delay in an advanced process (a few ps), unreachable with a plain inverter chain. This is the main battlefield of ADPLL literature for the past decade: (a) push Δtres\Delta t_{res}Δtres​ below a picosecond with interpolation, Vernier, or GRO (gated ring oscillator) techniques; (b) DTC assistance (digital-to-time converter: first shift the reference edge by the "predicted fractional phase", so the TDC only has to measure a tiny residual → a short, fine, linear TDC suffices); (c) simply use a bang-bang PD (1-bit TDC) — the quantization error is then no longer uniform white noise but is linearized by the input jitter (the KbbK_{bb}Kbb​ of the bang-bang CDR in this site's SerDes chapter is exactly that mechanism). All three roads share one goal: bring the (Δtres/TV)2(\Delta t_{res}/T_V)^2(Δtres​/TV​)2 term above down to the same order as SrefN2S_{ref}N^2Sref​N2.

Dimension check: as above; after 10log⁡1010\log_{10}10log10​ read as dBc/Hz — checks out; the inverse formula s×[1/Hz]⋅[Hz]=s\text{s}\times\sqrt{[1/\text{Hz}]\cdot[\text{Hz}]}=\text{s}s×[1/Hz]⋅[Hz]​=s — checks out.

import numpy as np
f0, fR = 5e9, 50e6
T_V = 1/f0
for dt_res in (10e-12, 20e-12):
    L_tdc = (2*np.pi)**2/12*(dt_res/T_V)**2/fR
    print(round(dt_res*1e12), "ps", f"{L_tdc:.4e}", round(10*np.log10(L_tdc), 2))
# -> 10 ps 1.6449e-10 -97.84
# -> 20 ps 6.5797e-10 -91.82
sigma_t = 10e-12/np.sqrt(12); sigma_phi = 2*np.pi*sigma_t/T_V
print(round(sigma_t*1e12, 3), round(sigma_phi*1e3, 2), f"{sigma_phi**2/fR:.4e}")
# -> 2.887 90.69 1.6449e-10 (sigma_t ps, sigma_phi mrad, sigma_phi^2/f_R = L_TDC)
L_cp = 0.5*1.5e-12
dt_eq = T_V*np.sqrt(12*L_cp*fR)/(2*np.pi)
print(round(10*np.log10(L_cp), 1), round(dt_eq*1e12, 3), round(10*np.log10(1.6449e-10/L_cp), 1))
# -> -121.2 0.675 23.4 (analog in-band floor ref×N² + CP in dBc/Hz, break-even dt_res ps, excess of the 10 ps TDC in dB)

Step 3: DCO frequency quantization → 1/Δf21/\Delta f^21/Δf2 skirt (varactor pipeline + ZOH)​

The DCO control word is updated once per reference period, and its finest bank is Δfres\Delta f_{res}Δfres​. The frequency the loop wants lies between two steps; the DCO can only take the nearest — the frequency quantization error efe_fef​ is uniform over ±Δfres/2\pm\Delta f_{res}/2±Δfres​/2. From here we follow Step 2 of the varactor page exactly, with the entry replaced from "KVCOvnK_{VCO}v_nKVCO​vn​" by "efe_fef​":

(i) Uniform frequency error. σf2=Δfres2/12\sigma_f^2=\Delta f_{res}^2/12σf2​=Δfres2​/12 [Hz²].

(ii) ZOH (zero-order hold) whitening at fRf_RfR​. The control word is constant within a reference period (held for TR=1/fRT_R=1/f_RTR​=1/fR​), so ef(t)e_f(t)ef​(t) is "a white sequence at rate fRf_RfR​ through a ZOH": the power σf2\sigma_f^2σf2​ spread over ±fR/2\pm f_R/2±fR​/2 (two-sided) gives density σf2/fR\sigma_f^2/f_Rσf2​/fR​, and the ZOH's squared magnitude response is sinc2(f/fR)\mathrm{sinc}^2(f/f_R)sinc2(f/fR​) (sinc(x)=sin⁡(πx)/(πx)\mathrm{sinc}(x)=\sin(\pi x)/(\pi x)sinc(x)=sin(πx)/(πx)):

SΔf(f)=Δfres212 1fR sinc2(ffR)[Hz2/Hz].S_{\Delta f}(f)=\frac{\Delta f_{res}^2}{12}\,\frac{1}{f_R}\,\mathrm{sinc}^2\Big(\frac{f}{f_R}\Big)\qquad[\text{Hz}^2/\text{Hz}].SΔf​(f)=12Δfres2​​fR​1​sinc2(fR​f​)[Hz2/Hz].

(iii) Frequency → phase: the same integrator. ϕ(t)=2π∫tef dt′\phi(t)=2\pi\int^t e_f\,dt'ϕ(t)=2π∫tef​dt′; in the power domain multiply by (2π)2/Δω2=1/Δf2(2\pi)^2/\Delta\omega^2=1/\Delta f^2(2π)2/Δω2=1/Δf2 (varactor page Step 2.3, the 2π2\pi2π cancels top and bottom):

LDCO(Δf)=112(ΔfresΔf)21fR sinc2(ΔffR),SDCO=2 LDCO\mathcal{L}_{DCO}(\Delta f)=\frac{1}{12}\Big(\frac{\Delta f_{res}}{\Delta f}\Big)^2\frac{1}{f_R}\,\mathrm{sinc}^2\Big(\frac{\Delta f}{f_R}\Big),\qquad S_{DCO}=2\,\mathcal{L}_{DCO}LDCO​(Δf)=121​(ΔfΔfres​​)2fR​1​sinc2(fR​Δf​),SDCO​=2LDCO​

(same factor-of-2 flag: 1/121/121/12 is the two-sided reading = the SSB number; this site's single-sided SϕS_\phiSϕ​ needs ×2\times2×2.)

(iv) Into the loop. It sits in the VCO's seat and is high-passed by ∣Hhp∣2\lvert H_{hp}\rvert^2∣Hhp​∣2 — inside fnf_nfn​ the loop corrects it away (just as it corrects the VCO's close-in drift), outside fnf_nfn​ it leaks out unchanged. Shape: for Δf≪fR\Delta f\ll f_RΔf≪fR​, sinc2≈1\mathrm{sinc}^2\approx1sinc2≈1 and LDCO∝1/Δf2\mathcal{L}_{DCO}\propto1/\Delta f^2LDCO​∝1/Δf2 — 20 dB down per decade, the same slope as the VCO's white-noise 1/f21/f^21/f2 skirt; near fR/2f_R/2fR​/2 the sinc2\mathrm{sinc}^2sinc2 pushes it down a bit further.

Dimension check: (Δfres/Δf)2(\Delta f_{res}/\Delta f)^2(Δfres​/Δf)2 [Hz²/Hz² = dimensionless] ×1/fR\times1/f_R×1/fR​ [1/Hz] ×sinc2\times\mathrm{sinc}^2×sinc2 [dimensionless] =1/Hz=1/\text{Hz}=1/Hz; phase is dimensionless (rad), so read as rad2/Hz\text{rad}^2/\text{Hz}rad2/Hz — checks out (the same unit argument as the varactor page's KVCO2Sv/Δf2K_{VCO}^2S_v/\Delta f^2KVCO2​Sv​/Δf2).

Division of labour with the ISF (the same sentence as the varactor page): Γ\GammaΓ handles "a current impulse Δq\Delta qΔq hitting the tank at a given phase → how much phase"; Δfres\Delta f_{res}Δfres​ handles "a quasi-static frequency step → how much phase after integration". Both roads converge on the same 1/Δω21/\Delta\omega^21/Δω2 integrator — that is what "the same bookkeeping" in this page's title means. The ISF has two further appearances inside a DCO: the DCO's own device noise SvcoS_{vco}Svco​ (Γrms2/qmax2\Gamma_{rms}^2/q_{max}^2Γrms2​/qmax2​, completely unchanged); and the charge kickback Δq\Delta qΔq injected into the tank when a unit capacitor switches — the phase at which it lands (Γ(ω0τ)\Gamma(\omega_0\tau)Γ(ω0​τ)) decides how much phase jump and spur the dither causes ([P1] operational definition Δϕ=ΓΔq/qmax\Delta\phi=\Gamma\Delta q/q_{max}Δϕ=ΓΔq/qmax​).

Worked example (Example 2: a DCO with Δfres=10\Delta f_{res}=10Δfres​=10 kHz)​

Example 2: f0=5f_0=5f0​=5 GHz, fR=50f_R=50fR​=50 MHz, Δfres=10\Delta f_{res}=10Δfres​=10 kHz (2 ppm). Find LDCO\mathcal{L}_{DCO}LDCO​ at Δf=0.1\Delta f=0.1Δf=0.1, 1, 10 MHz; convert to the ΔC\Delta CΔC of the finest unit capacitor (tank C=1C=1C=1 pF).

Step-by-step substitution (1 MHz):

  1. (Δfres/Δf)2=(104/106)2=10−4(\Delta f_{res}/\Delta f)^2=(10^4/10^6)^2=10^{-4}(Δfres​/Δf)2=(104/106)2=10−4 (dimensionless).
  2. ×1/12=8.333×10−6\times1/12=8.333\times10^{-6}×1/12=8.333×10−6; ×1/fR=8.333×10−6/(5×107)=1.667×10−13\times1/f_R=8.333\times10^{-6}/(5\times10^7)=1.667\times10^{-13}×1/fR​=8.333×10−6/(5×107)=1.667×10−13.
  3. ZOH: sinc2(106/5×107)=sinc2(0.02)=0.9987\mathrm{sinc}^2(10^6/5\times10^7)=\mathrm{sinc}^2(0.02)=0.9987sinc2(106/5×107)=sinc2(0.02)=0.9987 (−0.006-0.006−0.006 dB, negligible).
  4. LDCO(1 MHz)=10log⁡10(1.665×10−13)=−127.8\mathcal{L}_{DCO}(1\text{ MHz})=10\log_{10}(1.665\times10^{-13})=-127.8LDCO​(1 MHz)=10log10​(1.665×10−13)=−127.8 dBc/Hz.
  5. 0.1 MHz: ×100\times100×100 → −107.8-107.8−107.8; 10 MHz: ×1/100\times1/100×1/100 times sinc2(0.2)=0.875\mathrm{sinc}^2(0.2)=0.875sinc2(0.2)=0.875 (−0.58-0.58−0.58 dB) → −148.4-148.4−148.4 dBc/Hz. −20-20−20 dB per decade (plus the sinc extra as Δf→fR/2\Delta f\to f_R/2Δf→fR​/2).
  6. Unit capacitor: f0∝1/LCf_0\propto1/\sqrt{LC}f0​∝1/LC​ → Δf0/f0=−12ΔC/C\Delta f_0/f_0=-\tfrac12\Delta C/CΔf0​/f0​=−21​ΔC/C → ΔC=2C Δfres/f0=2×10−12×104/(5×109)=4.0\Delta C=2C\,\Delta f_{res}/f_0=2\times10^{-12}\times10^4/(5\times10^9)=4.0ΔC=2CΔfres​/f0​=2×10−12×104/(5×109)=4.0 aF.

Result and interpretation: −127.8-127.8−127.8 dBc/Hz at 1 MHz is 27.8 dB below the lab_20 ring VCO's −100-100−100 dBc/Hz — a ring-DCO does not care at all; but it is 20 dB above the site's canonical LC value of −148-148−148 dBc/Hz (Example B): a good LC-DCO would be drowned by its own quantization noise. And a 4 aF unit capacitor cannot be built physically (parasitics alone are two orders of magnitude larger) — so a DCO must be ΔΣ-dithered (Step 4): a buildable, coarser unit cell (tens of aF to fF) is toggled at a fast clock to buy fine "average" resolution.

Dimension check: ΔC=[F]×[Hz]/[Hz]=F\Delta C=[\text{F}]\times[\text{Hz}]/[\text{Hz}]=\text{F}ΔC=[F]×[Hz]/[Hz]=F — checks out.

import numpy as np
f0, fR, df_res, C = 5e9, 50e6, 10e3, 1e-12
for df in (1e5, 1e6, 1e7):
    L_dco = (1/12)*(df_res/df)**2/fR*np.sinc(df/fR)**2
    print(round(df/1e6, 1), f"{L_dco:.4e}", round(10*np.log10(L_dco), 2), round(10*np.log10(np.sinc(df/fR)**2), 2))
# -> 0.1 1.6666e-11 -107.78 -0.0
# -> 1.0 1.6645e-13 -127.79 -0.01
# -> 10.0 1.4586e-15 -148.36 -0.58 (MHz, linear, dBc/Hz, sinc^2 correction dB)
print(f"{2*C*df_res/f0*1e18:.1f}")
# -> 4.0 (finest unit capacitor, aF)

Step 4: ΔΣ dithering — shaping the DCO LSB up to high frequency​

Recipe: take a dither clock fdthf_{dth}fdth​ much faster than fRf_RfR​ (usually derived by dividing CKV, e.g. f0/8f_0/8f0​/8), and use an mmm-th-order ΔΣ modulator to turn the "desired fractional frequency" into an on/off sequence for one physical unit cell. First separate two "resolutions" that are easy to confuse:

  • Unit-cell step Δfu\Delta f_uΔfu​: how far the frequency jumps when the dithered physical capacitor toggles once. Use the conversion of Example 2, Δfu=f0 ΔCu/(2C)\Delta f_u=f_0\,\Delta C_u/(2C)Δfu​=f0​ΔCu​/(2C) [Hz]. This is one step of the modulator output.
  • Averaged (effective) resolution Δfeff=Δfu/2W\Delta f_{eff}=\Delta f_u/2^{W}Δfeff​=Δfu​/2W: a WWW-bit fractional control word lets the duty of the unit cell be trimmed finely, so the long-term average frequency can sit on a grid of Δfu/2W\Delta f_u/2^WΔfu​/2W. It only decides "how accurately the average frequency can be placed" (the static frequency error); it does not enter the noise formula.

The shaped noise power is set by the step of the modulator output, i.e. Δfu\Delta f_uΔfu​ — not by the averaged Δfeff\Delta f_{eff}Δfeff​. The reason is direct: in any one clock period the unit cell is either fully on or fully off, so the instantaneous frequency error is of order Δfu\Delta f_uΔfu​; the ΔΣ modulator does not make this error smaller, it only moves its spectrum to high frequency.

Step-by-step derivation (external literature, not among this site's 5 PDFs; the algebra is that of the ΔΣ third term in pll_noise_budget, except that what is shaped is frequency and the sampling rate is fdthf_{dth}fdth​):

(i) Modulator output and error. The input x[k]x[k]x[k] is the desired fraction (unit: cell, 0≤x<10\le x\lt10≤x<1) and the output v[k]v[k]v[k] is an integer number of cells. An mmm-th-order modulator satisfies v=x+(1−z−1)mev=x+(1-z^{-1})^m ev=x+(1−z−1)me, where eee is the quantizer error, uniformly distributed over ±12\pm\tfrac12±21​ cell in the white-noise model: σe2=1/12\sigma_e^2=1/12σe2​=1/12 [cell²].

(ii) Convert to frequency. Each cell is worth Δfu\Delta f_uΔfu​ [Hz/cell], so the variance of the frequency error is σf2=Δfu2/12\sigma_f^2=\Delta f_u^2/12σf2​=Δfu2​/12 [Hz²].

(iii) Whitening at fdthf_{dth}fdth​, shaping, ZOH. One sample per dither period spreads the power over ±fdth/2\pm f_{dth}/2±fdth​/2 (two-sided) → density σf2/fdth\sigma_f^2/f_{dth}σf2​/fdth​; the squared magnitude of (1−z−1)m(1-z^{-1})^m(1−z−1)m is ∣1−e−j2πf/fdth∣2m=[2sin⁡(πf/fdth)]2m\lvert1-e^{-j2\pi f/f_{dth}}\rvert^{2m}=[2\sin(\pi f/f_{dth})]^{2m}∣1−e−j2πf/fdth​∣2m=[2sin(πf/fdth​)]2m (dimensionless); the cell state is held for 1/fdth1/f_{dth}1/fdth​ (ZOH), which multiplies by sinc2(f/fdth)\mathrm{sinc}^2(f/f_{dth})sinc2(f/fdth​):

SΔf(f)=Δfu212 1fdth[2sin⁡(πffdth)]2msinc2(ffdth)[Hz2/Hz].S_{\Delta f}(f)=\frac{\Delta f_{u}^2}{12}\,\frac{1}{f_{dth}}\Big[2\sin\Big(\frac{\pi f}{f_{dth}}\Big)\Big]^{2m}\mathrm{sinc}^2\Big(\frac{f}{f_{dth}}\Big)\qquad[\text{Hz}^2/\text{Hz}].SΔf​(f)=12Δfu2​​fdth​1​[2sin(fdth​πf​)]2msinc2(fdth​f​)[Hz2/Hz].

(iv) Frequency → phase. Through the same 1/Δf21/\Delta f^21/Δf2 integrator as in Step 3:

LDCO,ΔΣ(Δf)=112(ΔfuΔf)21fdth[2sin⁡(πΔffdth)]2msinc2(Δffdth).\mathcal{L}_{DCO,\Delta\Sigma}(\Delta f)=\frac{1}{12}\Big(\frac{\Delta f_{u}}{\Delta f}\Big)^2\frac{1}{f_{dth}}\Big[2\sin\Big(\frac{\pi\Delta f}{f_{dth}}\Big)\Big]^{2m}\mathrm{sinc}^2\Big(\frac{\Delta f}{f_{dth}}\Big).LDCO,ΔΣ​(Δf)=121​(ΔfΔfu​​)2fdth​1​[2sin(fdth​πΔf​)]2msinc2(fdth​Δf​).

(The same factor-of-2 flag: 1/121/121/12 is the two-sided reading = the SSB number; this site's single-sided SϕS_\phiSϕ​ needs ×2\times2×2.)

(v) Low-offset approximation. For Δf≪fdth\Delta f\ll f_{dth}Δf≪fdth​, 2sin⁡(πΔf/fdth)≈2πΔf/fdth2\sin(\pi\Delta f/f_{dth})\approx2\pi\Delta f/f_{dth}2sin(πΔf/fdth​)≈2πΔf/fdth​ and sinc2≈1\mathrm{sinc}^2\approx1sinc2≈1:

LDCO,ΔΣ≈(2π)2m12 Δfu2 Δf 2m−2fdth 2m+1,m=1:  L≈π23 Δfu2fdth3  (independent of Δf).\mathcal{L}_{DCO,\Delta\Sigma}\approx\frac{(2\pi)^{2m}}{12}\,\frac{\Delta f_u^{2}\,\Delta f^{\,2m-2}}{f_{dth}^{\,2m+1}},\qquad m=1:\ \ \mathcal{L}\approx\frac{\pi^2}{3}\,\frac{\Delta f_u^2}{f_{dth}^3}\ \ (\text{independent of }\Delta f).LDCO,ΔΣ​≈12(2π)2m​fdth2m+1​Δfu2​Δf2m−2​,m=1:  L≈3π2​fdth3​Δfu2​​  (independent of Δf).

Three effects stacked together:

  • m=0m=0m=0 (just toggle faster, no shaping): the power Δfu2/12\Delta f_{u}^2/12Δfu2​/12 is spread over ±fdth/2\pm f_{dth}/2±fdth​/2; it is still a 1/Δf21/\Delta f^21/Δf2 skirt, only 10log⁡10(fdth/fR)10\log_{10}(f_{dth}/f_R)10log10​(fdth​/fR​) lower than "the same step updated once per 1/fR1/f_R1/fR​".
  • m=1m=1m=1: the +20+20+20 dB/dec shaping exactly cancels the integrator's −20-20−20 dB/dec → L\mathcal{L}L becomes a flat floor ∝Δfu2/fdth3\propto\Delta f_u^2/f_{dth}^3∝Δfu2​/fdth3​: −6-6−6 dB per halving of the unit cell, −9-9−9 dB per doubling of fdthf_{dth}fdth​. A flat floor set against the 1/Δf21/\Delta f^21/Δf2 skirt of the DCO's thermal noise always overtakes it beyond some offset, so what matters is "where the crossover falls".
  • m=2m=2m=2: a net +20+20+20 dB/dec climb — lower than m=1m=1m=1 at low offset, a higher hump at high offset. DCO quantization noise travels the high-pass path: beyond fnf_nfn​ the loop does not attenuate it at all, the hump appears at the output unchanged, and only the sinc null at fdthf_{dth}fdth​ and downstream filtering can hold it down. This is the key difference between DCO dither and fractional-N divider dither — the latter is a low-pass path where the loop cuts the high end. A second-order modulator (e.g. MASH 1-1) has an output spanning 4 levels, so 3 unit cells are dithered together; the step in the formula is still the single-cell Δfu\Delta f_uΔfu​. Hence the DCO side usually uses only first or second order and pushes fdthf_{dth}fdth​ high.

Dimension check: Δfu2/Δf2\Delta f_u^2/\Delta f^2Δfu2​/Δf2 [dimensionless] ×1/fdth\times1/f_{dth}×1/fdth​ [1/Hz], all other factors dimensionless → rad2/Hz\text{rad}^2/\text{Hz}rad2/Hz — checks out; the approximation Hz2⋅Hz2m−2/Hz2m+1=1/Hz\text{Hz}^2\cdot\text{Hz}^{2m-2}/\text{Hz}^{2m+1}=1/\text{Hz}Hz2⋅Hz2m−2/Hz2m+1=1/Hz — checks out.

Caveat on the white-noise model: eee is white only when the modulator input is "busy" or dither is added. A first-order modulator fed a static input produces idle tones (discrete lines): the total power is unchanged but it is not a flat floor (see D3 in the numerical verification).

Worked example (Example 3: 40 aF and 1 fF unit cells, dither at f0/8f_0/8f0​/8)​

Example 3: continue with the tank of Example 2 (f0=5f_0=5f0​=5 GHz, C=1C=1C=1 pF). Two buildable unit cells: ΔCu=40\Delta C_u=40ΔCu​=40 aF and 111 fF. fdth=f0/8=625f_{dth}=f_0/8=625fdth​=f0​/8=625 MHz. Find LDCO,ΔΣ\mathcal{L}_{DCO,\Delta\Sigma}LDCO,ΔΣ​ at Δf=1\Delta f=1Δf=1 MHz and 10 MHz for m=0,1,2m=0,1,2m=0,1,2, and compare with the thermal-noise skirt of the LC-DCO (Example B: −148.0-148.0−148.0 dBc/Hz at 1 MHz, 1/Δf21/\Delta f^21/Δf2).

Step-by-step substitution:

  1. Unit-cell step: Δfu=f0ΔCu/(2C)\Delta f_u=f_0\Delta C_u/(2C)Δfu​=f0​ΔCu​/(2C). 40 aF → 5×109×40×10−18/(2×10−12)=1005\times10^9\times40\times10^{-18}/(2\times10^{-12})=1005×109×40×10−18/(2×10−12)=100 kHz; 1 fF → 2.52.52.5 MHz. (The 10 kHz of Example 2 does not appear here: it is only a target for the averaged resolution; a 40 aF cell with W=4W=4W=4 bits gives 100/24=6.25100/2^4=6.25100/24=6.25 kHz and a 1 fF cell with W=8W=8W=8 bits gives 2500/28=9.772500/2^8=9.772500/28=9.77 kHz, both reachable.)
  2. m=0m=0m=0, 1 MHz, 40 aF: (105/106)2/12/(6.25×108)=1.333×10−12(10^5/10^6)^2/12/(6.25\times10^8)=1.333\times10^{-12}(105/106)2/12/(6.25×108)=1.333×10−12 → −118.8-118.8−118.8 dBc/Hz. The 1 fF step is 25 times larger (+27.96+27.96+27.96 dB) → −90.8-90.8−90.8 dBc/Hz.
  3. Shaping factor: 2sin⁡(π×106/6.25×108)=2sin⁡(5.027×10−3)=1.0053×10−22\sin(\pi\times10^6/6.25\times10^8)=2\sin(5.027\times10^{-3})=1.0053\times10^{-2}2sin(π×106/6.25×108)=2sin(5.027×10−3)=1.0053×10−2; squared 1.011×10−41.011\times10^{-4}1.011×10−4 (−40.0-40.0−40.0 dB). m=1m=1m=1: 40 aF → −158.7-158.7−158.7, 1 fF → −130.7-130.7−130.7 dBc/Hz. Cross-check with the approximation: (π2/3)(105)2/(6.25×108)3=1.347×10−16(\pi^2/3)(10^5)^2/(6.25\times10^8)^3=1.347\times10^{-16}(π2/3)(105)2/(6.25×108)3=1.347×10−16 → −158.7-158.7−158.7 — checks out.
  4. m=2m=2m=2: multiply by the shaping factor once more. 1 MHz: 40 aF → −198.7-198.7−198.7, 1 fF → −170.7-170.7−170.7; 10 MHz (shaping factor +20+20+20 dB): 40 aF → −178.7-178.7−178.7, 1 fF → −150.7-150.7−150.7 dBc/Hz.
  5. LC-DCO thermal noise (Example B): −148.0-148.0−148.0 at 1 MHz, −168.0-168.0−168.0 dBc/Hz at 10 MHz. Bookkeeping-family flag: this is the /4/4/4 (SSB bookkeeping) family of [P1] Eq.(21); the /2/2/2 family (that of [P2] Eq.(6)) gives −145.0-145.0−145.0. The table below uses the stricter −148.0-148.0−148.0; with the /2/2/2 family every difference moves 3 dB in the favourable direction and the conclusions are unchanged.

Result (quantization noise − thermal noise; positive = quantization noise is higher):

Unit cell (Δfu\Delta f_uΔfu​)mmm1 MHzvs −148.0-148.0−148.010 MHzvs −168.0-168.0−168.0Crossover with thermal noise
40 aF (100 kHz)1−158.7-158.7−158.7−10.7-10.7−10.7 dB−158.7-158.7−158.7+9.3+9.3+9.3 dBovertakes beyond 3.43 MHz
40 aF (100 kHz)2−198.7-198.7−198.7−50.7-50.7−50.7 dB−178.7-178.7−178.7−10.7-10.7−10.7 dBovertakes beyond 18.5 MHz
1 fF (2.5 MHz)1−130.7-130.7−130.7+17.3+17.3+17.3 dB−130.8-130.8−130.8+37.3+37.3+37.3 dBovertakes beyond 0.14 MHz
1 fF (2.5 MHz)2−170.7-170.7−170.7−22.7-22.7−22.7 dB−150.7-150.7−150.7+17.3+17.3+17.3 dBovertakes beyond 3.69 MHz

Interpretation (the honest version):

  • Whether first-order dither is enough depends on how large the unit cell is. A 40 aF cell sits 10.7 dB below the LC thermal noise at 1 MHz; a 1 fF cell sits 17.3 dB above it — first-order dither cannot rescue a 1 fF cell, and the LC-DCO's −148-148−148 is buried by its own quantization noise.
  • How small is small enough? Taking "10 dB below thermal noise" as the criterion: f0/8f_0/8f0​/8, m=1m=1m=1 needs Δfu≤108\Delta f_u\le108Δfu​≤108 kHz (ΔCu≤43\Delta C_u\le43ΔCu​≤43 aF) at 1 MHz; if 10 MHz must hold as well, it needs Δfu≤10.8\Delta f_u\le10.8Δfu​≤10.8 kHz (4.3 aF) — back to an unbuildable size.
  • How to rescue a 1 fF cell? Raise the order and the dither frequency together: m=2m=2m=2, fdth=f0/2=2.5f_{dth}=f_0/2=2.5fdth​=f0​/2=2.5 GHz gives −200.8-200.8−200.8 at 1 MHz and −180.8-180.8−180.8 dBc/Hz at 10 MHz (12.8 dB below −168.0-168.0−168.0; under the same conditions the cell limit is 1.38 fF). Raising only the order (m=2m=2m=2, f0/8f_0/8f0​/8) is overtaken beyond 3.69 MHz; raising only the frequency (m=1m=1m=1, f0/2f_0/2f0​/2) gives a flat −148.8-148.8−148.8 dBc/Hz, just level with the thermal noise at 1 MHz.
  • The 40 aF cell: m=1m=1m=1, f0/2f_0/2f0​/2 relaxes the limit for holding 10 MHz to 35 aF (just short); m=2m=2m=2, f0/8f_0/8f0​/8 is 10.7 dB below at 10 MHz, with the crossover at 18.5 MHz.
  • The price: the unit cell switches every 1.6 ns (f0/8f_0/8f0​/8), and each switching event is a Δq\Delta qΔq hitting the tank — the ISF says the phase at which it lands decides how much the phase jumps (Δϕ=Γ(ω0τ)Δq/qmax\Delta\phi=\Gamma(\omega_0\tau)\Delta q/q_{max}Δϕ=Γ(ω0​τ)Δq/qmax​); when fdthf_{dth}fdth​ is synchronous with f0f_0f0​ these jumps repeat at fixed phases, one of the sources of spurs. The formula only accounts for the "quantization" share; the dither clock's own jitter, kickback spurs and cell-to-cell mismatch are separate.

Dimension check: Δfu=[Hz]×[F]/[F]=Hz\Delta f_u=[\text{Hz}]\times[\text{F}]/[\text{F}]=\text{Hz}Δfu​=[Hz]×[F]/[F]=Hz — checks out; the rest as above.

import numpy as np
f0, C = 5e9, 1e-12
f_dth = f0/8
def L_q(df_u, df, m, fd=f_dth):
    return (1/12)*(df_u/df)**2/fd*(2*np.sin(np.pi*df/fd))**(2*m)*np.sinc(df/fd)**2
def L_th(df):
    return 0.25/1e-12**2*1e-24/(4*(2*np.pi*df)**2)       # [P1] Eq.(21), /4 family
dB = lambda x: round(float(10*np.log10(x)), 1)
print(dB(L_th(1e6)), dB(L_th(1e7)), dB(2*L_th(1e6)))
# -> -148.0 -168.0 -145.0 (thermal noise at 1 MHz, 10 MHz; the /2 family at 1 MHz)
for dC in (40e-18, 1e-15):
    df_u = f0*dC/(2*C)
    print(round(dC*1e18), round(df_u/1e3), [dB(L_q(df_u, 1e6, m)) for m in (0, 1, 2)],
          [dB(L_q(df_u, 1e7, m)) for m in (1, 2)])
    print([dB(L_q(df_u, d, m)/L_th(d)) for m in (1, 2) for d in (1e6, 1e7)])
# -> 40 100 [-118.8, -158.7, -198.7] [-158.7, -178.7]
# -> [-10.7, 9.3, -50.7, -10.7]
# -> 1000 2500 [-90.8, -130.7, -170.7] [-130.8, -150.7]
# -> [17.3, 37.3, -22.7, 17.3] (aF, kHz, m=0,1,2 at 1 MHz, m=1,2 at 10 MHz; the following line is the difference to thermal noise in dB)
print(dB(np.pi**2/3*1e5**2/f_dth**3), dB(4), dB(8))
# -> -158.7 6.0 9.0 (m=1 approximation; dB gained per halving of the cell and per doubling of f_dth)
for fd, m, d in ((f0/8, 1, 1e6), (f0/8, 1, 1e7), (f0/2, 1, 1e7), (f0/2, 2, 1e7)):
    df_u = 1e5*np.sqrt(0.1*L_th(d)/L_q(1e5, d, m, fd))   # 10 dB below thermal
    print(round(fd/1e6), m, round(d/1e6), round(df_u/1e3, 1), round(2*C*df_u/f0*1e18, 1))
# -> 625 1 1 108.4 43.4
# -> 625 1 10 10.8 4.3
# -> 2500 1 10 86.7 34.7
# -> 2500 2 10 3450.4 1380.2 (f_dth MHz, m, offset MHz, step upper limit kHz, cell upper limit aF)
print(dB(L_q(2.5e6, 1e6, 2, f0/2)), dB(L_q(2.5e6, 1e7, 2, f0/2)), dB(L_q(2.5e6, 1e6, 1, f0/2)))
# -> -200.8 -180.8 -148.8 (1 fF: m=2 at f0/2 at 1 and 10 MHz; m=1 at f0/2)
print([round(x) for x in (1e5/2**4, 2.5e6/2**8)])
# -> [6250, 9766] (averaged resolution in Hz: 40 aF with 4 bits, 1 fF with 8 bits)
from scipy.optimize import brentq
print([round(brentq(lambda d: np.log(L_q(u, d, m)/L_th(d)), 1e4, 2e8)/1e6, 2)
       for u, m in ((1e5, 1), (1e5, 2), (2.5e6, 1), (2.5e6, 2))])
# -> [3.43, 18.5, 0.14, 3.69] (crossover offset with the thermal skirt, MHz)

Step 5: the ADPLL budget equation and a worked example​

Putting the two new sources into the framework of pll_noise_budget:

Sout(f)=(SrefN2+STDC)∣Hlp∣2+(SDCO+Svco)∣Hhp∣2.S_{out}(f)=\big(S_{ref}N^2+S_{TDC}\big)\lvert H_{lp}\rvert^2+\big(S_{DCO}+S_{vco}\big)\lvert H_{hp}\rvert^2 .Sout​(f)=(Sref​N2+STDC​)∣Hlp​∣2+(SDCO​+Svco​)∣Hhp​∣2.
  • STDCS_{TDC}STDC​ replaces ScpS_{cp}Scp​ (same seat, same low-pass, same "no N2N^2N2"); SDCOS_{DCO}SDCO​ sits beside SvcoS_{vco}Svco​ (same seat, same high-pass). The fractional-N ΔΣ third term does not exist in an ADPLL — the fractional frequency is handled directly by the fractional accumulation of RRR_RRR​, with no divider dithering; but TDC nonlinearity turns the periodic pattern of the fractional part of RRR_RRR​ into fractional spurs (see applicability and failure).
  • ∣Hlp∣2,∣Hhp∣2\lvert H_{lp}\rvert^2,\lvert H_{hp}\rvert^2∣Hlp​∣2,∣Hhp​∣2 are the type-II second-order closed loop of pll_noise_budget (the digital loop filter's zzz-domain implementation agrees with its continuous-time approximation for f≪fRf\ll f_Rf≪fR​).

Example 4: use the lab_20 SrefS_{ref}Sref​ and SvcoS_{vco}Svco​ of pll_noise_budget (ring toy, Lvco(1 MHz)=−100\mathcal{L}_{vco}(1\text{ MHz})=-100Lvco​(1 MHz)=−100 dBc/Hz), N=100N=100N=100, ζ=0.707\zeta=0.707ζ=0.707, plus the STDCS_{TDC}STDC​ of Example 1 (10 ps and 1 ps) and the SDCOS_{DCO}SDCO​ of Example 2 (undithered). (a) Spot value at Δf=1\Delta f=1Δf=1 MHz with fn=1f_n=1fn​=1 MHz; (b) integrated jitter (1 kHz–1 GHz) at fn=6.9f_n=6.9fn​=6.9 MHz (the analog optimum); (c) the ADPLL's own optimum fnf_nfn​.

Step by step (spot, 10 ps):

  1. In-band term: SrefN2=10−12S_{ref}N^2=10^{-12}Sref​N2=10−12, STDC=2×1.645×10−10=3.29×10−10S_{TDC}=2\times1.645\times10^{-10}=3.29\times10^{-10}STDC​=2×1.645×10−10=3.29×10−10 (single-sided); ∣Hlp(1 MHz)∣2=1.50\lvert H_{lp}(1\text{ MHz})\rvert^2=1.50∣Hlp​(1 MHz)∣2=1.50 (peaking) → 4.95×10−104.95\times10^{-10}4.95×10−10.
  2. Out-of-band term: SDCO=2×1.665×10−13=3.33×10−13S_{DCO}=2\times1.665\times10^{-13}=3.33\times10^{-13}SDCO​=2×1.665×10−13=3.33×10−13, Svco=2×10−10S_{vco}=2\times10^{-10}Svco​=2×10−10; ∣Hhp∣2=0.50\lvert H_{hp}\rvert^2=0.50∣Hhp​∣2=0.50 → 1.00×10−101.00\times10^{-10}1.00×10−10.
  3. Total 5.95×10−105.95\times10^{-10}5.95×10−10 → L=10log⁡10(12×5.95×10−10)=−95.3\mathcal{L}=10\log_{10}(\tfrac12\times5.95\times10^{-10})=-95.3L=10log10​(21␀​×5.95×10−10)=−95.3 dBc/Hz. The TDC term alone is 83% — it even buries the ring VCO.
  4. 1 ps: STDCS_{TDC}STDC​ drops 100× → in-band 6.4×10−126.4\times10^{-12}6.4×10−12, the total is VCO-dominated → −102.7-102.7−102.7 dBc/Hz.

Architecturefnf_nfn​σt\sigma_tσt​Reading
Analog CP-PLL (Scp=5×10−13S_{cp}=5\times10^{-13}Scp​=5×10−13)6.9 MHz259 fspll_noise_budget optimum

Interpretation: this is the numerical version of "why an ADPLL needs a fine TDC / DTC assistance / BB-PD". A 10 ps TDC pushes the optimum jitter from 259 fs to 1 ps and forces you to narrow the BW by 15× — a disaster for a noisy ring-DCO; only a 1 ps TDC returns to the same order of magnitude. Conversely, the (undithered) SDCOS_{DCO}SDCO​ is invisible in this ring toy (28 dB lower); it only surfaces with an LC-DCO, and that is when the dither of Step 4 is needed — and the unit cell must be small enough (Example 3; the LC-DCO version of the budget is in the numerical verification of the next section).

Dimension check: ∫Sout df\int S_{out}\,df∫Sout​df [rad²] → σϕ/(2πf0)\sigma_\phi/(2\pi f_0)σϕ​/(2πf0​): rad/(rad/s) = s — checks out.

import numpy as np
from simulations.common.pll_utils import H_lowpass_mag2, H_highpass_mag2
f0, fR, N = 5e9, 50e6, 100
T_V = 1/f0
f = np.logspace(3, 9, 3000)
S_ref = 1e-16 + 1e-18*(1e6/f)                       # same table as pll_noise_budget
S_vco = 2e-10*(1e6/f)**2                            # ring toy, L(1 MHz) = -100 dBc/Hz
S_dco = 2*(1/12)*(1e4/f)**2/fR*np.sinc(f/fR)**2     # single-sided = 2 L_DCO
def S_tdc(dt_res):
    return 2*(2*np.pi)**2/12*(dt_res/T_V)**2/fR     # single-sided = 2 L_TDC
def sigma_t(S_out):
    return np.sqrt(np.trapezoid(S_out, f))/(2*np.pi*f0)
fn = 1e6
lp1, hp1 = H_lowpass_mag2(np.array([1e6]), fn)[0], H_highpass_mag2(np.array([1e6]), fn)[0]
for dt in (10e-12, 1e-12):
    inb = (1e-12 + S_tdc(dt))*lp1
    outb = (S_dco[np.argmin(abs(f-1e6))] + 2e-10)*hp1
    print(round(dt*1e12), f"{inb:.3e}", f"{outb:.3e}", round(10*np.log10(0.5*(inb + outb)), 1))
# -> 10 4.950e-10 1.002e-10 -95.3
# -> 1 6.435e-12 1.002e-10 -102.7 (dt_res ps, in-band, out-of-band rad^2/Hz, L dBc/Hz)
fn = 6.9e6
lp, hp = H_lowpass_mag2(f, fn), H_highpass_mag2(f, fn)
print(round(sigma_t((S_ref*N**2 + 5e-13)*lp + S_vco*hp)*1e15))
# -> 259 (analog CP-PLL, fs)
for dt in (10e-12, 1e-12):
    print(round(dt*1e12), round(sigma_t((S_ref*N**2 + S_tdc(dt))*lp + (S_dco + S_vco)*hp)*1e15))
# -> 10 2773
# -> 1 363 (ADPLL at f_n = 6.9 MHz, fs)
fns = np.logspace(4.5, 7.5, 60)
for dt in (10e-12, 1e-12):
    jit = [sigma_t((S_ref*N**2 + S_tdc(dt))*H_lowpass_mag2(f, x) + (S_dco + S_vco)*H_highpass_mag2(f, x)) for x in fns]
    k = int(np.argmin(jit))
    print(round(dt*1e12), round(fns[k]/1e6, 2), round(jit[k]*1e15))
# -> 10 0.47 1001
# -> 1 3.84 338 (ADPLL's own optimum f_n MHz, sigma_t fs)

Numerical verification (lab_44: time-domain simulation of the quantization noise)​

Both quantization-noise formulas above rest on the model "the error is white". simulations/lab_44_adpll_quantization.py generates the quantization-error sequences directly in the time domain, estimates their PSD and compares with the formulas; it also puts the unit cells of Example 3 into the budget of an LC-DCO (Example 4 uses the ring toy, where DCO quantization is invisible).

  • When the white-noise model holds, the formulas are accurate to within 1%, and the step that goes into them is indeed the unit-cell Δfu\Delta f_uΔfu​ (100 kHz, 2.5 MHz) — the two sets of curves in panel (b) differ by 20log⁡1025=2820\log_{10}25=2820log10​25=28 dB, exactly the square of the step ratio.
  • Three ways the white-noise assumption fails:
    • T2 (noiseless fractional ramp): the rms of the error is still Δtres/12\Delta t_{res}/\sqrt{12}Δtres​/12​ (ratio 1.00), but it is a periodic sawtooth and 94% of the power sits in 10 lines; the strongest is −26.0-26.0−26.0 dBc before loop filtering (sawtooth fundamental: peak phase 2Δtres/TV=0.12\Delta t_{res}/T_V=0.12Δtres​/TV​=0.1 rad). This is a fractional spur — present even with a perfectly linear TDC; the "flat floor" requires a random component comparable to Δtres\Delta t_{res}Δtres​ in the input, or dither.
    • T3 (integer-N, static offset, jitter far below one step): the TDC output code takes 1 value only — there is no quantization "noise", the TDC simply cannot see the phase moving (dead zone); a real loop drifts to a code boundary and turns into a bang-bang-like limit cycle, which is no longer what this formula describes.
    • D3 (first-order ΔΣ, static input): the phase variance equals that of the white-noise model (ratio 1.00), but 94% of it sits in idle tones; the strongest is 20log⁡10(Δfu/fdth)20\log_{10}(\Delta f_u/f_{dth})20log10​(Δfu​/fdth​): 1 fF → −48.0-48.0−48.0 dBc, 40 aF → −75.9-75.9−75.9 dBc.
  • The lesson of D4: a dither one cell wide added before the quantizer breaks the tones up into white noise, but the dither itself is shaped as part of the error and the power doubles (1/12→1/61/12\to1/61/12→1/6, +3+3+3 dB). Second order (D2) is already white enough even with a static input.

Limitations (honest statement):

  • The simulation is an open-loop error sequence, not a closed-loop time-domain ADPLL simulation; panel (c) and the table above are the analytic formulas inserted into the type-II continuous-time ∣H∣2\lvert H\rvert^2∣H∣2, with no digital latency and no zzz-domain effects.
  • The quantizer is ideal (no DNL/INL, no metastability); the unit cell is ideal (no mismatch, no switching kickback, no jitter on the dither clock). In real circuits these often become the limit before the "quantization" share does.
  • The simulated curves in panel (b) depart from the formula above 100 MHz: the simulation estimates the phase sampled at fdthf_{dth}fdth​, aliasing included, while the formula is a continuous-time spectrum. The ratios are taken only inside the 0.5–2 MHz band.
  • The integration runs to 1 GHz with no far-out white floor of an output buffer; the 1/f21/f^21/f2 skirt of a real LC oscillator does not keep falling to −200-200−200 dBc/Hz, so the absolute 20 fs-class values in the table are optimistic — the ranking and the order-of-magnitude gaps are the trustworthy part.
  • The thermal noise uses the /4/4/4 family's −148.0-148.0−148.0; with the /2/2/2 family (−145.0-145.0−145.0) the σt\sigma_tσt​ of the thermal term is multiplied by 2\sqrt22​ and the quantization rows are unchanged.

Connection to SerDes​

The ADPLL's output σt\sigma_tσt​ (Example 4) feeds the eye diagram and BER of serdes_clocking_connection exactly as an analog PLL's does. Two ADPLL-specific reminders: (1) the TDC floor is flat white noise all the way to fR/2f_R/2fR​/2, so under a wide BW its contribution to integrated jitter grows linearly ∝fn\propto f_n∝fn​ (less "afraid" of narrowing the BW than a 1/f21/f^21/f2 source, more afraid of widening it); (2) the latency of the digital loop (TDC conversion and digital filtering each take a few reference periods) reduces phase margin and raises peaking — the "cascaded 0.1 dB" rule of pll_noise_budget must include latency in an ADPLL (external literature, beyond this page). The bang-bang CDR in a SerDes is in fact an ADPLL with a "1-bit TDC": the BB-PD linearized gain KbbK_{bb}Kbb​ mentioned in Example 1 is that road.

Key takeaways​

  • An ADPLL replaces PFD/CP with a TDC and the VCO with a DCO; phase is counted in VCO cycles, ϕE=RR−RV−ε\phi_E=R_R-R_V-\varepsilonϕE​=RR​−RV​−ε.
  • TDC quantization = in-band white floor (PFD seat, low-pass, no N2N^2N2): LTDC=(2π)212(ΔtresTV)21fR\mathcal{L}_{TDC}=\dfrac{(2\pi)^2}{12}\Big(\dfrac{\Delta t_{res}}{T_V}\Big)^2\dfrac{1}{f_R}LTDC​=12(2π)2​(TV​Δtres​​)2fR​1​ (two-sided reading = SSB number; this site's single-sided SϕS_\phiSϕ​ needs ×2\times2×2). f0=5f_0=5f0​=5 GHz, fR=50f_R=50fR​=50 MHz: 10 ps → −97.8-97.8−97.8, 20 ps → −91.8-91.8−91.8 dBc/Hz; breaking even with the analog in-band floor of −121.2-121.2−121.2 (ref×N² + CP) needs 0.6750.6750.675 ps.
  • DCO quantization = white frequency noise through a ZOH → integrate → 1/Δf21/\Delta f^21/Δf2 skirt (VCO seat, high-pass): LDCO=112(ΔfresΔf)21fRsinc2(ΔffR)\mathcal{L}_{DCO}=\dfrac{1}{12}\Big(\dfrac{\Delta f_{res}}{\Delta f}\Big)^2\dfrac{1}{f_R}\mathrm{sinc}^2\Big(\dfrac{\Delta f}{f_R}\Big)LDCO​=121​(ΔfΔfres​​)2fR​1​sinc2(fR​Δf​); 10 kHz at 1 MHz → −127.8-127.8−127.8 dBc/Hz, −20-20−20 dB per decade; corresponds to ΔC=4\Delta C=4ΔC=4 aF (unbuildable → dither).
  • ΔΣ dither: the same (1−z−1)m(1-z^{-1})^m(1−z−1)m with the sampling rate swapped for fdthf_{dth}fdth​, and the step that goes into the formula is that of the dithered physical unit cell, Δfu=f0ΔCu/(2C)\Delta f_u=f_0\Delta C_u/(2C)Δfu​=f0​ΔCu​/(2C), not the averaged resolution. m=1m=1m=1 lets the +20+20+20 shaping cancel the −20-20−20 integration → a flat floor ∝Δfu2/fdth3\propto\Delta f_u^2/f_{dth}^3∝Δfu2​/fdth3​; example: f0/8f_0/8f0​/8, m=1m=1m=1 at 1 MHz, 40 aF (100 kHz) → −158.7-158.7−158.7, 1 fF (2.5 MHz) → −130.7-130.7−130.7 dBc/Hz — the latter 17.3 dB above the LC-DCO's −148.0-148.0−148.0 (/4/4/4 family), so first order is not enough; a 1 fF cell needs m=2m=2m=2 and fdth=f0/2f_{dth}=f_0/2fdth​=f0​/2 (−200.8-200.8−200.8 / −180.8-180.8−180.8 at 1 / 10 MHz), or the cell must shrink below 43 aF. The DCO path is high-pass, the loop does not cut the high-frequency hump — the key difference from fractional-N divider dither; a higher order improves the spot value yet can worsen the integrated jitter (188.5 → 230.7 fs).
  • Numerical verification (lab_44): when the white-noise model holds the formulas are accurate to 1%; a noiseless fractional ramp and a first-order ΔΣ with a static input give spurs / idle tones (94% of the power in 10 lines), not a flat floor.
  • Budget: Sout=(SrefN2+STDC)∣Hlp∣2+(SDCO+Svco)∣Hhp∣2S_{out}=(S_{ref}N^2+S_{TDC})\lvert H_{lp}\rvert^2+(S_{DCO}+S_{vco})\lvert H_{hp}\rvert^2Sout​=(Sref​N2+STDC​)∣Hlp​∣2+(SDCO​+Svco​)∣Hhp​∣2; Example 4: a 10 ps TDC pushes the optimum σt\sigma_tσt​ from 259 fs to 1001 fs and narrows the BW to 0.47 MHz; only 1 ps returns to 338 fs — the raison d'être of fine TDCs / DTC assistance / BB-PDs.
  • The ISF term (Svco∝Γrms2/qmax2S_{vco}\propto\Gamma_{rms}^2/q_{max}^2Svco​∝Γrms2​/qmax2​) is unchanged, word for word, inside a DCO; the ISF additionally decides how much spur the dither switching kickback Δq\Delta qΔq causes depending on the phase at which it lands.
  • Every time you write 1/121/121/12, flag it: that is two-sided bookkeeping = the SSB number; this site's single-sided SϕS_\phiSϕ​ is 1/61/61/6.
